steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Colonel Hamilton, I hope you understand what you've done.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: What I've done? I've succeeded in defeating Victoria's enemies, and brought us an all too rare victory.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: You truly think you'll win?

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: We have eradicated the rabble occupying the city hall and our other important facilities. You can hear it, can't you? Our troops are taking back the city, bit by bit.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Suppose things do go as you intend, the spectre force never recovers from this, and you successfully defend County Hillock—

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: You will still have brought Victoria a terrible, irreconcilable defeat!

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: What nonsense are you spouting? I see. You're still soft on those commoners.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Let me say this again, Skamandros. This is war, and victory comes hand in hand with bloodshed.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Enough rationalizing your actions. The locals here have always been part of your plan.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: When you ordered the artillery battalion to make those dirty bombs in secret, the spectre force wasn't anywhere close to infiltrating County Hillock!

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Not one to give up easily, are we?

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: But fine. All has gone without a hitch, and there's no opportunity left for you to get in the way.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Without a hitch? Because you fanned the flames of war you saw before you?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: War is not an end, but a means.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: The wars we fought over the past decades were meant to safeguard Victoria's peace and prosperity. But you? In an afternoon, you laid waste to lifetimes of hard work.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: How dare you blindly attack the common folk in the name of the Victorian Army? Regardless of ancestry, these people are still Victorian citizens!

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: They call themselves Tarans!

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: And how much of our country's population is Taran? One-tenth? One-fifth?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Right. You see them in the minority, but when the ire of so many is set alight, it could very well burn down the whole Empire!

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Hmph. They stand no chance against the might of the Victorian Army.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: They should never have had a need for that chance!

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Look at that book you're reading. You marvel at the achievements of the first Aslan king, but did you ever consider what it was that propelled a foreign Aslan to become ruler of Victoria?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: If the Aslans hadn't signed an armistice with the Dracos, and if the Draco King Gaeil hadn't yielded to the royal family's decision, the Victoria we know today would never have existed in the first place!

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: What right do you have—to push Victoria to the brink of civil war once again, all for your own hatred and prejudice?!

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Do you really believe everything you've just spouted, Skamandros?

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Do you really believe that I, the commander of a single garrison in the countryside, could steer the Empire of Victoria with a wave of my hand?

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Have you ever wondered, why... why Londinium is so deafeningly silent?

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: I could have killed you. Even being the noble you are, Londinium would never hold me accountable for the death of a lieutenant to rebel cannon fire.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: But I didn't. I respect your loyalty to Victoria, and I cannot bear to see so-called human nature blunt Her blades.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Open your eyes. The war began long ago! And until the last of our enemies lies dead, we will never have true victory!

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Have you ever considered that all you do could be playing right into those enemies' hands?

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: What you fear is, in fact, my greatest hope—

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: I wish for the fate of the Tarans to be known across all of Victoria!

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: It is not the people I want to destroy. No, I look to destroy their courage.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: I want the whole world to know that, should they dare to turn against us, they must be prepared to withstand the fire of Victoria's rage!

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: How much innocent blood will it take to douse these flames you started today?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Grand dukes with sinister motives, all the surrounding countries with their hidden agendas, and the outsiders teeming with ambition—

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: —With all these ill-meaning sides gathered in one spot, Londinium, maybe even all of Victoria, endures far more pressure than one place should bear.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: All those parties, biding their time, need just one little push, and, bang—

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: The fire will spread, and it won't stop at the Tarans, it will spread all across the once-prosperous lands, sparing no one in its path.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: And how... is that worse than letting the parasites chew you hollow from the inside-out, not doing a thing to stop them?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: It seems there's no going back for you.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: In that case, we have nothing further to discuss.

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Perfect, then. I have no need to keep you locked up here. Away with you, if you please.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Once you release me, I will make sure you answer for your crimes.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: I swear this on Triangle's team—No matter what happens, as long as I live, I will see you court martialed!

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Hah. You think that's enough to frighten me?

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Listen, Skamandros. If Victoria wishes to lay down judgement, She knows where to find me.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: And I can't wait to see it done.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Cello, Oboe, we're making for the communications center.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: If Bagpipe fails to escort the Messenger out of the city, then that will be our last chance, and we must seize it.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Considering the situation, the communications center has most likely fallen to the enemy. This will be a difficult battle.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: But we've never been the type to shy away.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Forward, soldiers of Victoria! We do this for Triangle now, for her team!

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: What's the situation?

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: I'm not getting a response—Hill?

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: You're not here. How dare you desert your post?

steps.name: Colonel Hamilton
steps.text: Where did you go without my specific instruction?!

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Phew... There's way too many wounded here...

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: We need to get the ones with light wounds into the buildings that are still standing. Anyone with more serious injuries or symptoms should be taken to the closest clinic—Remember to quarantine them.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: There aren't enough beds in the clinics.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: District Seventeen, the Taran quarter, suffered the worst of the damage in the bombardment.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Some residents cleared out an area to set up a few tents with a few dozen beds, to act as a temporary base.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: I've passed on all the prevention methods you've taught me, and a few volunteers are moving the less gravely injured to the tents now.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: As soon as I finish taking care of the first aid supplies we have left here, I'll go join them.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: You're good at this, and they trust you too.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Haha... One of the things I learned in the army over the years is how to make friends.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: They always tell me the guards of honor are the face of the military, and I never doubted it. I've got used to them praising Victoria's glory and prosperity with their applause and cheers.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: That's definitely part of what Victoria means, say what they will.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: But it's not... the whole story.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: After the conversation we had, I remembered some things from ages ago I'd forgotten.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: My da's a lawyer, and he used to tell me stories about how my grandda's grandda came to Victoria with nothing. He went from rags to riches.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: The Victoria he described was an advanced, open-minded, prosperous country.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Here, technology and capital conquered savagery. The people's hard work and wealth wouldn't be destroyed just like that by Catastrophes or racial conflict.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: In making it to such a magnificent land, we Vouivre were able to live a 'civilized' life, compared to one of barbarism and violence in the old country.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Victoria was the most advanced industrialized nation in the world, for a very long time..

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: But we had to give up a lot, in order to become Victorians...

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: When I was five, I climbed to the top of the tallest tree in our garden. My da caught me having a blast and gave me a good scolding.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Then he locked me in my room and gave me dozens of books to read. The next day, he hired a Leithanian piano teacher for me.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: I missed the view from the top of the tree, but I didn't give it much thought. I knew my da was doing it for my own good.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: He was helping you to get used to the rules.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: That's right. Books, piano, the garden... He understood that those were all things we'd need to know, in order to enjoy the life we had.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: And, I also remembered another thing...

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: This one time after school, I saw a few older kids bullying a young Feline girl behind my favorite bakery.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: They laughed at her, saying her clothes were dirty and that she didn't know anything.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: After they left, I went up to her and gave her a few novels I had in my school bag.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: I thought she'd be able to talk to the kids her age once she finished reading them, and the others wouldn't pick on her anymore...

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: About a week later, I was all excited, went looking for her so we could talk about the books, but she just shook her head and handed them back to me.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: I could tell right away. She never even flipped them open. I was really mad. Here I was trying to befriend her, lending her my books, and she wouldn't even accept my kindness.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: It wasn't until much later, I realized...

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: She couldn't read.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: She was the child of a bakery worker, not even a baker. How was she supposed to get an education? Forget enjoying any of the same things you did.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: It turns out, even being able to read a novel is a luxury.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Victoria's always been an unequal society, hasn't it?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: I wasn't willing to accept that before... I'd let myself grow accustomed to the 'rules,' and that was how I became a proper Victorian. And those who live outside the rules, well, our country would never accept them.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: It takes courage to open your mind on your own like that.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Waking up from a dream of a glorified imagination of a civilization, shaped by a people's collective consciousness isn't easy. Trust me, I know that better than anyone.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Because you're from Laterano?

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Because I left Laterano.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: If we get the chance, I'm hoping to hear about your past... instead of having you listen to the silly troubles of an ordinary girl.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: You're not ordinary, Jane. No one should call herself ordinary.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Thanks. All your comfort's keeping me from wasting away, honestly, wallowing in my misery.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: You've never stopped putting in the effort to do your best work.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: I've got everything packed. I'll take it over to the temporary medical base now.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Stay alert on the way.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Right. The whole city's in chaos. Thankfully, the garrison's stopped attacking, and the rioters have mostly dispersed. As long as the citizens can band together, there's still hope for County Hillock.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Man is far stronger than we can ever imagine. A lot of ambitious types find themselves on the wrong side of history when they underestimate that.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: *Sigh*. The biggest problem is we don't have enough medicine.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: We can at least clean and bandage their wounds.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: I still have medicine with me. I don't need the ones you've shared just yet.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: If I can use some of it, we might be able to save a few more souls.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Put it back. Don't even think about it.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Make sure you're safe before you go saving anyone else. So you can save even more of those who need saving.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Yeah... Okay, I got it.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: I'll come back once I'm done delivering this.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: We've taken care of most of the wounded here.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Are you going to head to the other side of the statue?

steps.name: Operator Fred
steps.text: Oi, Lass, I'm scoping the area with my binoculars, and I'm seeing an injured girl not far away from where you are.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Any details?

steps.name: Operator Fred
steps.text: She's young. I can't make out her race... Vouivre, maybe?

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: How is she looking?

steps.name: Operator Fred
steps.text: Not good. I think I see a huge Originium shard sticking through her abdomen. Chances are she's infected now. Looks like she's lost too much blood and passed out as well.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: I'm heading there now.

steps.name: Operator Fred
steps.text: Wait... Lass, that's an active warzone!

steps.name: Operator Fred
steps.text: I don't see any hostiles nearby, but that area was taken over by the rioters not long ago. Besides, the building right behind her is their command center!

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: So?

steps.name: Operator Fred
steps.text: That wounded lass is very likely one of their key personnel.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Since when has Rhodes Island cared about sides when providing aid to those in need?

steps.name: Operator Fred
steps.text: Sorry. This isn't a judgement I can make... Oliver, have you been listening in?

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: Yes... Lass, I'm not prepared to act rashly either. If she has to do with this whole mess, it might be risky for our company.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: I get it. You see someone at the center of a power struggle, and who just got infected.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: What I see instead is an Infected who is gonna die in the power struggle afterwards.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: And before she finally dies, a whole bunch of other struggles will swirl around her, sending even more to their deaths.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: But as long as there's still a glimmer of hope that I can stop that ugly mess, I can't give up.

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: Lass... I can't talk you out of it... but I will follow your lead.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: No, Oliver, I'm in no position to give you orders, and I certainly don't want to.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: But remember, and make sure you write this in your after action report—

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: This isn't a Rhodes Island elite operator making a call. This is Outcast's personal decision.

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Right, and don't forget your 'but.'

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: 'Temporary Operator Outcast did not follow the officer-in-charge's evacuation orders and opted to rescue an individual who constituted a security risk.' Something like that.

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: Say what you want, even... Forget Rhodes Island. You're putting yourself in serious danger!

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: And that is why we can't drag even more people into this mess.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: It's better if Rhodes Island has nothing to do with this operation. You and your operators can follow the original plan. As soon as the rescue operation is done, you get out of County Hillock with all the documents.

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: Lass... I'll stay with you.

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: Shredder?!

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: Oliver, feel free to add another note to the report, that you fired me here on the spot.

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: You've got to be out of your mind!

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: Okay, yeah... Fine. Go. You're saving an Infected, aren't you? That's Rhodes Island's bread and butter!

steps.name: Operator Oliver
steps.text: I'm not leaving without any one of you. Get to the rendezvous point on time!

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Thanks, Oliver. You're a great leader.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Shredder, I appreciate the help, but I hope you'll take my advice.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: That is—Stay here.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: I'll go by myself. Whatever happens, do not come after me. Go straight to the rendezvous point.

steps.name: Operator Shredder
steps.text: Right... I'll be there.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Outcast...

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Jane, you aren't trying to stop me, are you?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Are you really going to save her? I heard she was one of the rioters' central figures...

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: She might even be the one who killed Saoirse!

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Honestly, I doubt a mysterious group with big plans would leave their true leader to die on the street.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Phew... That's alright, then... I—I feel much better now.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: But what if she was the one who killed her? What would you do? Would you ask me to leave her to die?

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: To tell the truth... I don't know.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: But I agree with what you said. She's a poor Infected girl who desperately needs our help.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: I guess I might ask her once she's out of danger...

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Never mind, I'm probably overthinking it. I'll stop wasting your time.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Off I go then.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Hold on. One more thing...

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: Remember what you told me? Make sure you're safe yourself before you help anyone else!

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Well, lookie here. Our little Janie's trying to educate me.

steps.name: Janie
steps.text: No... I wouldn't presume to...

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: Don't worry.

steps.name: Outcast
steps.text: It's just as we said—I'm saving a regular old Infected.
